notes: Building and Engineering News, vol. 16 part 1 (Internet Archive buildingengineer1616cont), the 26 weekly issues from 5 January to 28 June 1916. Same method as the later volumes: every numbered entry under Building Permit Applications and Building Contracts was taken from the djvu.xml OCR, East Bay headings set aside, and each San Francisco lot built from the block corner on the DPW street centrelines and compared with the sf-parcels shapes; a placement was accepted where the lot starts within two feet of a lot line of today (or the record names an unambiguous corner) and the roll dates the building 1915-1918, and alterations were matched by printed street number in sf-eas-addresses where the roll dates the building before 1916. The labels are printed with leader dots and each item is printed once. The OCR garbles many item numbers in this volume, so extract.py was run with BEN_LOOSE=1, which also takes an entry under a type heading whose number it cannot read; the item numbers of the published rows were then read from the page image, and unresolved rows whose number was not read carry no extra.item and say so in the locator. A few issues print numbers out of sequence (877 to 939 in late February and early March); they are recorded as printed. Every published row was read against the page image, location first; a cost or name that could not be read on the image was left out. Descriptions of rows marked confidence low were built from the OCR and have not been read against the image. Owners are private individuals and are cut everywhere (raw.note; scrub_owner.py removes the fragments the OCR garbles past the first cut); a firm or institution named as owner is kept, and where the contractor, architect or designer named is the owner, shares the owner's surname or is listed at the owner's own address or beside the building site that name is cut too, with the owner firm. Sub-trade contracts are timeline entries and set no builder credit; the builder credit set from a steam heater room at 1459 Jones Street (1201 Jackson Street) was taken off again. Completion notices, liens, sub-contracts printed 'on above' and the news columns were not taken. The paper came out on Wednesdays; issue dates are set from the cover dates (issues.json beside the corpus: first leaf of each issue, set by hand from the mastheads two or four leaves after each cover), and the dated running heads agree with them. Seven single houses that were read against the image and have no architect or no name left to publish sit with the held single houses. One held fact whose parcel got a page from this volume was read: a 1931 listing placed at 1827 Mason Street is an Alameda address and stays held.

coverage.remaining: Vols. 16 pt. 1 to 31 read (January 1916 to January 1932); the 2 half-year volumes of 1915 are unread, buildingengineer15215cont next. In this volume: 133 rows placed on a parcel whose roll year fits, single houses with no architect named and no page, are logged and held until another fact gives the parcel a page (extra.placed_apn; all but seven still need the image check). 229 rows have a nearest parcel that was not accepted (the lot starts off today's lot lines, or the roll dates the building outside the window). 530 rows were not placed: location lines not parsed (tract lots, garbled headings), street pairs that do not cross under the names read, and printed street numbers with no EAS row today. About 180 more numbered items were not extracted at all because the OCR lost both the number and the owner label.
coverage.note: 1,753 numbered entries read, 1,033 San Francisco rows, 503 placed on a parcel, 148 picked and read against the page image, 98 published on 95 pages (45 seeded), 43 held back: 30 storeys, unit counts or uses that contradict the roll, 8 pieces of minor work and 5 alterations with nothing to confirm the street number; seven more joined the held houses.
